newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal not to raise taxes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Portugal not to raise taxes in 1997.

text.p: Portugal's 1997 budget proposals do not include tax increases and forecast privatisation revenues of 500 billion escudos ($3.2 billion), Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Thursday.
"The 1997 budget will not raise taxes, as happened in 1996," Sousa Franco said during a parliamentary debate on the planned European single currency.

He said the government expected to earn 500 billion escudos from privatisations in 1997, which should help it to meet targets to reduce the public debt and budget deficit in order to qualify to join a single currency.

Socialist Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said in New York this month that the state could raise 450 billion escudos ($2.91 billion) from privatisations in 1996, well above its target of 380 billion ($2.46 billion).
Sousa Franco said the 1997 budget to be presented to parliament on October 15 would be rigorous with a social conscience.
Analysts said the Socialists should pass the budget through parliament in a vote in November.
The government has said the budget deficit should fall to 2.9 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997 from around four percent in 1996.
It has forecast that the ratio of public debt to GDP should be around 68 percent in 1997, down from 69 to 70 percent in 1996.

Sousa Franco said the level of unemployment appeared to be stagnating. It stood at 7.1 percent of the workforce in the third quarter, compared with 7.2 percent in the second quarter and 6.9 percent in the third quarter of 1995.
